title: C8_OFFLINE_RELIABILITY_BINS
universal_lens: Offline reliability binning establishes a structural isomorphism between discrete empirical frequency spaces and continuous predictive probability manifolds. By partitioning the unit hypercube into equal-width bins, we measure Expected Calibration Error (ECE), quantifying the L1 divergence between predicted expectations and realized outcomes, serving as a foundational metric for probabilistic system honesty.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, offline ECE acts as a conformal calibration layer over Bayesian posterior predictive distributions. It measures the discrepancy between model-issued confidence intervals and actual event frequencies on settled fixtures, ensuring that our probabilistic forecasts maintain rigorous statistical coverage without relying on external market priors.
gse_mapping: For GSE, this primitive maps to situational state-transition validation. The binned reliability metrics verify that internal engine probabilities accurately reflect physical outcome frequencies across distinct tactical regimes, acting as a strict gatekeeper before any operator UI exposes these probabilities to downstream decision-making systems.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation of the Offline Reliability Bins operator begins with the fundamental requirement of probabilistic coherence: a predicted probability must asymptotically match the observed relative frequency. We define a partition of the unit interval [0,1] into B equal-width bins, denoted as I_b. For each prediction p_hat_i assigned to a specific fixture, we map it to its corresponding bin b. Within each bin, we calculate the empirical frequency f_emp,b = (1/N_b) * sum(y_i), where y_i is the binary realization. The Expected Calibration Error (ECE) is then formulated as the weighted L1 distance: ECE = sum_{b=1}^B (N_b / N) * |f_emp,b - p_avg,b|, where p_avg,b is the average predicted probability in bin b. This operator acts as a dual to the maximum likelihood estimation; while MLE optimizes for sharpness, ECE optimizes for honesty. The failure mode arises when the binning strategy imposes artificial discretization artifacts, particularly in sparse regions of the probability space. To mitigate this, the scaffold enforces a strict 'no public performance publish' rule until the ECE converges below a predefined threshold. This ensures that the downstream LRD-style operator only interfaces with a calibrated probability manifold, preventing the propagation of overconfident or miscalibrated priors into the strategic reasoning layers of the GSE.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to the foundational works of Brier (1950) on the verification of forecasts and Dawid (1982) on prequential principles. Historically, reliability diagrams were introduced to visually inspect the alignment between forecasters' confidence and reality. In modern quantitative finance and sports intelligence, this evolved into rigorous Expected Calibration Error metrics used to audit black-box machine learning models, ensuring they do not hallucinate certainty where none exists.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a theory of mind perspective, the ECE operator models the 'honesty' of the predictive agent (the model). It assumes the opposing agent (the real world or the market) will exploit any miscalibration. If the model consistently overestimates probabilities in a specific bin, a rational adversary will construct a Dutch Book against it. Thus, minimizing ECE is equivalent to achieving Nash equilibrium in a game against a perfectly informed nature, ensuring the model's outputs are robust to exploitation.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical cross-layer veto condition is applied here: if the ECE exceeds a tolerance epsilon, the system triggers a hard block on the PERFORMANCE_STATS flip. This prevents leakage of uncalibrated signals into the public UI. Furthermore, we enforce anti-collinearity by ensuring that the binning edges do not align systematically with known feature thresholds (e.g., home/away splits), which could mask localized miscalibrations behind globally acceptable ECE scores.
